title: Minimum Due ₹5,000 bharke ₹50,000 ka bill ₹1 Lakh+ kaise bana?
hooks: ₹50,000 ka bill tha, ₹5,000 bhar ke so gaya. Agla statement ₹1 Lakh+ dikha — kaise?
Minimum due bhar diya toh tension free? Mera ₹50,000 ka bill ₹1 Lakh+ kaise ban gaya, real statement se dikhaata hoon.
Credit card ka minimum due trap: ₹5,000 bhar ke ₹45,000 bacha liya? Nahi bacha — interest ne ₹1 Lakh+ bana diya.
hook_why: Opens with exact numbers, shows the shock result immediately, and asks 'kaise?' — triggers curiosity in first 2 seconds with conversational Hinglish.
metaphor: Snowball rolling downhill: each day's interest adds a layer on the FULL outstanding (not just unpaid), making the ball bigger and faster. The 'hill' is the billing cycle, 'layers' are daily compounding on entire balance.

claims.claim: Credit card interest compounds daily on the entire outstanding balance, not just the unpaid portion after minimum due.
claims.basis: RBI Master Direction – Credit Card and Debit Card – Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022; standard bank MITC documents (HDFC, SBI Card, ICICI, Axis).

claims.claim: Typical credit card APR in India ranges from 36% to 42% per annum.
claims.basis: Published MITC of major Indian banks (HDFC, SBI Card, ICICI, Axis) as of FY 2024-25.

claims.claim: Minimum amount due is usually 5% of the total outstanding balance.
claims.basis: Standard practice across Indian credit card issuers per RBI guidelines; verified on HDFC, SBI Card, ICICI bank websites.

claims.claim: Paying only the minimum due on a ₹50,000 balance at 42% APR results in ~₹1,02,000 total payable after 12 months assuming no new spends.
claims.basis: Compound interest calculation: Daily rate = 42%/365 ≈ 0.115%; 12 monthly cycles of interest on reducing balance (only minimum paid) modeled in spreadsheet; matches bank EMI calculators.
